items.notes:
I checked every finding against the code by running the model with vite-node, and against /home/user/sources/t1_lrm_clean.txt (§12.4.1 around line 20066, §12.4.2 / §12.4.2.1 around lines 20130-20213, §12.5 and Syntax 12-3 around lines 20329-20402, §12.5.1, §12.5.2, §12.5.3 / §12.5.3.1 around lines 20529-20601, §12.5.4 around line 20628). All 16 in-scope findings reproduced as described.

Decisions:
- F2: I chose the wording option, not the 'not reached' status option. The item status and the 'no match' badge stay, because they are true statements about the values and changing the status would change behaviour. The 'fit the select' wording also goes into the correct run feedback (not only the summary and the plain silentBecause), so the summary, the feedback and the badge agree. Two pinned strings are unchanged on purpose: the wrong-later-item sentence ('X does match under casez, but Y matches earlier in source order') and the priority silentBecause. Neither claims the later item was compared.
- F3: The finding suggested scoping the legend by form. I scoped it by what the chip tables actually draw (via the shared drawsChips predicate), following docs/visual-learning/visual-language.md, which says a legend lists only what the figure draws. This gives the outcome the finding asked for and more: plain case also drops '– skipped', since only casez and casex skip; case inside and if chains never show '–'; '? wildcard' appears only when a wildcard is drawn; and the '? is written z' note appears only when a compared literal contains a '?'. One existing assertion changed for that reason: the lesson-decoder legend is now 'Chips: 1 match, 0 mismatch.'
- F11: I did not drop the if-chain stamp entirely. It is still needed for ==? and range conditions, whose explanations never say that an x condition is false. It is now dropped only when a bit or an == term in the item already states the rule. The sweep shows every if-chain x pick states the rule exactly once.
- F7: DEFERRED_REPORT_NOTE is kept, now documented as the case-form line, because tests import it. Nothing outside my four files imports it; I grepped src, tests and content.
- F16: I cited §12.5.1 alone rather than adding a case inside half. The WILDCARD_ASYMMETRY_NOTE, which follows it in the same paragraph, already states the case inside rule.
- F13: Exact-count asserts became floors (at least 14,336 and at least 7,072) so that adding a preset does not fail the test for the wrong reason. To check the sweep is not vacuous, I removed the card deduplication in a scratch run: 34 listed-value configurations then failed.

Rejected: none. Not mine: F5 (content/.../flow-control.mdx). The lesson's 'every value matches something' / 'the default matches every value' wording and its §12.5.3 NOTE citation are still for the lesson workflow.

No other behaviour changed. Every outcome, match count and report kind is the same: the full sweeps and every pinned outcome test pass unchanged.
s3: S3 src/components/visuals/DecisionLab.tsx:804 (marks from src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:735) - The F3 legend scoping is only partly done. chipMarks also counts chip tables that sit inside closed plain-miss folds, so the legend can list a mark no visible table draws. Example: preset lrm-priority-inside (case inside) at the listed value 001. The only open table is 1 (3'b001), and it shows only 1s. Item 2 (3'b0?0, [4:7]) is folded. The legend still reads '? wildcard in the item. A ? in the source is written z here'. A sweep over presets x forms x all selects found 17 such cases (for example casez/casex 001 and 011 list '- skipped' only from folds). The legend is never missing a mark that is drawn. -> Build the marks from the tables that are unfolded, and add a fold's terms only while that fold is open (ChipScope already tracks open folds through details[data-chips][open]). Otherwise, change the ChipScope doc to say that folded tables count.

S3 src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:997 - The F2 vocabulary split stops partway. Under plain and priority, a wrong pick of a later fitting item still says it 'does match'. Example: the priority-encoder preset as shipped, req=1111, pick item 2: '4'b??1? does match under casez, but 4'b???1 matches earlier in source order'. Beside it, the correct answer now says '4 casez items fit the select'. tests/lib/sv-decision-model.test.ts:1694 is titled 'no reachable text calls the later items matches under plain or priority'. That overclaims: allTexts includes this feedback and the term whys, its regex just misses them, and test line 844 pins 'does match' under plain. No rule is wrong. -> When !reportsOverlap(qualifier), word it as '... also fits the select (would match), but the search stopped at <first>' ('holds' in an if chain). Otherwise, retitle the test to name only the summary, silentBecause and correct-answer feedback.

S3 src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:775 - 'fit the select' is wrong for a constant-expression case. Take one-hot (case (1'b1)), edit the qualifier to plain or priority, and set gnt=011. The output reads '2 case items fit the select (gnt[0], gnt[1])' right after 'gnt[0] is 1, which matches the case expression 1'b1 (§12.5.2)'. The items are compared with 1'b1, not with the select gnt; the model's own doc at :665 says the case expression is 1'b1 there. -> Use 'fit the case expression' (or 'would match'), or branch on result.constantExpression.

S3 src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:769-773 (also the laterMatchBadge doc at :869-872) and tests/lib/sv-decision-model.test.ts:1678 - The rationale says 'unique and unique0 keep comparing after the first match ... so the later items do match', and the test title says unique and unique0 'compare them all'. That overstates IEEE 1800-2023 §12.5.3, which says that after a uniqueness violation is found the implementation is not required to keep comparing (LRM text around line 20544; §12.4.2 around line 20164). With 3 or more fitting items, the items after the second match need not be compared. Example: priority-encoder edited to unique at req=1111 gives '4 case items match', and items 3 and 4 get the badge 'matches, not run'. The learner text is still true as a statement about values. -> Reword the comments and the test title to 'compares at least until a second match', and don't treat 'match' as meaning 'was compared' for the third and later items.

S3 src/components/visuals/DecisionLab.tsx:402 - TermDetail still picks the == or ==? verdict-row label with its own /[xXzZ?]/ regex. It should use the new shared usesWildcardEquality helper (src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:252), which conditionText and the x-stamp logic now use. As written, the chip table's verdict row could drift from the written condition. -> Use usesWildcardEquality(term.term).

S3 src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:775 - fitVerb's 'fit the select' is wrong for a constant-expression case. Take one-hot (case (1'b1)), set the qualifier to plain or priority, and set gnt = 3'b101. The summary reads '2 case items fit the select (gnt[0], gnt[2]).', silentBecause reads 'gnt[0], gnt[2] both fit the select', and the correct-run feedback reads '2 case items fit the select, and the first one in source order wins (§12.5)'. Those items are bits of the select and are compared with the case expression 1'b1, which their own cards say ('matches the case expression 1'b1 (§12.5.2)'). The rule and the outcome are right; only the wording is off. Reachable only by editing the preset, but priority case (1'b1) is the standard idiom. -> For the case family say 'fit the case expression', or 'fit 1'b1' when result.constantExpression is true, and pin the one-hot plain and priority text.

S3 tests/lib/sv-decision-model.test.ts:320 - The title 'no reachable text calls the later items matches under plain or priority' overclaims. Under plain, the wrong-pick feedback still says '2'b?1 does match under casez, but 2'b1? matches earlier in source order.' (pinned at :844, built at src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:997). The later item's term text also says '2'b?1 matches: casez skips bit 1 (§12.5.1)'. The regex checks only the count sentences, so one reveal now uses three phrasings for the same item: 'fit the select', 'does match' and 'would also match'. -> Retitle to 'the count sentences (summary, silence, correct answer) do not call ...', or apply fitVerb to the wrong-pick line too (e.g. '2'b?1 also fits the select under casez, but 2'b1? matches earlier in source order').

S3 src/components/visuals/DecisionLab.tsx:804 (also :1017; chipMarks at src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:735) - Question. chipMarks also counts chip tables inside closed plain-miss folds, so while the legend is visible it can name a mark that no open table draws. Example: lrm-priority-inside at status = 3'b001 under its own case inside. The legend reads '... ? wildcard in the item. A ? in the source is written z here (same bit value).', but the only open table (item 1, '1, 3') has neither. 14 preset/form/value states do this, including case-inside 0x0 and 0z0, where 'x unknown' comes only from a closed fold. -> Either compute the marks from open tables plus open folds (ChipScope already listens to fold toggles), or state in the ChipScope/chipMarks doc that the legend also covers folded tables.

S3 src/components/visuals/DecisionLab.tsx:402 - TermDetail still uses its own /[xXzZ?]/ regex to choose the '==?' or '==' verdict-row label. The new usesWildcardEquality helper (src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:252) names the same rule and now drives conditionText and the x-stamp dedupe. -> Use usesWildcardEquality(term.term) so the chip-table label and the feedback cannot drift apart.

items.notes:
LRM verification (in /home/user/sources/t1_lrm_clean.txt):
- §12.5 (from about line 20393) says a default case_item is ignored during the linear search, and the default statement runs if all comparisons fail. This supports every reworded 'takes no part in the comparisons / runs when every comparison fails' sentence.
- §12.5.3 (from about line 20553) says unique and priority shall issue a violation report if no case_item matches, and unique0 shall not.
- The §12.5.3 NOTE says only that with unique or priority you do not need to code a default to trap unexpected case values. It does NOT say that a default matches every leftover value, or that it makes 'no match' impossible. Every citation of the NOTE for that claim was removed or moved: the old lines 176, 474 and 965. The NOTE is now cited only for 'unique and priority trap unexpected values without a default' (lines 180, 482, 975).
- §12.4.2 (about line 20134) says a violation report is issued if no condition matches 'unless there is an explicit else'. It is cited for the if-chain case.
- Case-side citation: the decision model itself (noMatchClause, src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts:133-140) says §12.5.3 alone does not state the default exception; it follows from §12.5 plus the grammar, where default is a case_item. So the lesson cites '§12.5, §12.5.3' for 'with a default there is no no-match report', the same as the lab.

Searched the whole file for 'matches every', 'leftover', 'every value', 'matches something' and 'NOTE'. All instances of the error are fixed: the old lines 176, 224, 474, 962, 963, 965 and 1056.

Kept as is:
- Line 185, 'a default where every leftover value has a sensible meaning'. It is about design intent, not matching.
- Line 890 (now about 898), interview feedback 'A default silences the no-match check for every value ... (§12.5.3)'. It is accurate.

Placement decisions:
- Compare lab: put in '### case inside' right after the four-row casex / case inside table, not in Push Further. The casex-vs-inside preset is exactly that table, and the lab's per-bit chips lead into the 'Which bits count?' table that follows.
- Qualifiers lab: given an explicit preset="lesson-decoder" (it is also the default) so the embed stays tied to the decoder traced above it even if preset order changes.
- No content was removed apart from the incorrect wording.

Rejected or out of scope:
- The other S3 items in lastRoundS3 concern src/lib/sv-decision-model.ts, DecisionLab.tsx and tests. They are not my files and were not touched.
- No test reads this lesson's prose. tests/components/DecisionLab.test.tsx:926 checks that the lab itself does NOT show 'matches every leftover value', which agrees with this change.

No git operations, generators or builds were run.
s3: S3 content/curriculum/T1_Foundational/F2C_Procedural_Code_and_Flow_Control/flow-control.mdx:180 (same citation at :482, :970, :973, :1064) - The rule 'with a default, unique and priority issue no no-match report' is cited to (§12.5, §12.5.3). Neither clause says it. §12.5.3 (t1_lrm_clean.txt ~20552-20556) only says unique/priority report 'if no case_item matches' and never mentions default. The only explicit exemption in IEEE 1800-2023 is §12.4.2 (~20135-20136, 'unless there is an explicit else'), and it covers if chains only. Read literally, §12.5.3 next to the lesson's new sentence 'the default takes no part in the comparisons' (§12.5, ~20398) even suggests a report would be issued. So the 'So ...' in :180 does not follow from §12.5. What the lesson teaches is correct (tools behave this way, and the §12.5.3 NOTE treats a default and unique/priority as alternative ways to trap unexpected values), so the fault is the citation, not the rule. -> At :180, state the basis plainly in your own words: §12.5.3 phrases the check as no case item matching and is silent about default; §12.4.2 states the same rule explicitly for a final else; the NOTE presents default and unique/priority as alternative traps; simulators issue no report when a default runs. Drop the 'So'. In the quiz, Kata and pitfalls row, cite (§12.4.2, §12.5.3 NOTE) or point back to this bullet instead of presenting §12.5.3 as the source.

I checked the lesson against the lab by running the model itself (compareDecisions, via a vite-node script in the scratchpad using an alias config; no repo files touched):
- casex column: 0x0 runs NOP, 001 RW, 101 ALU, 110 ALU, 111 JUMP, 011 default, 1x0 ALU.
- case inside column: 0x0 default (item results x; 0,x; x; 0), 001 RW, 101 ALU, 110 ALU with 3'b11? marked 'matches, not run', 111 JUMP, 011 default, 1x0 default (range x, 3'b11? x).
- casez column: 0x0 and 1x0 both reach default.
All of these agree with the six-row trace (L369-376), the four-forms table (L355-360) and the casex remark at L378. I found no disagreement, so no existing lesson text needed fixing.

I checked the nearby text against the 1800-2023 LRM:
- §11.4.13 (t1_lrm_clean.txt ~L18291): integral members are compared with ==?; x/z on the left are not don't-cares; the result is x when nothing matches and some comparison is x (the OR reduction); $ bounds; unpacked arrays; == for non-integral values.
- §12.5.4 (~L20628): asymmetric wildcard matching; the case expression is the left operand; 1'b0 and 1'bx are no match.
- §11.4.6 (~L17715): wildcards apply only in the right operand.
- §11.4.4 (~L17602): a relational operator with an x or z operand gives 1'bx.

One soft spot I left alone: L364 says a range is 'tested with the relational operators >= and <='. The LRM only requires the bounds to be of a type for which <= and >= are defined, and says a match is found when the value lies inclusively within the range. It never states outright that an x in the value makes a range compare x. The model and the backlog modelRules take the same reading, and it changes no branch here (both 0x0 and 1x0 reach default either way). Rewording it would be a separate, optional precision edit.

I did not run generators, builds or git commands, and edited only the assigned file.
